McLaren.summary: McLaren has added extra “furniture” to the rear wing – basically small winglets that smooth and shape the airflow behind the car. This gives a bit more grip and stability, especially in fast corners, so the driver can push harder without the car getting unsettled. In short, the tweak should translate into quicker lap times and a more confident race‑day performance.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has trimmed the central element of the rear wing and added a small winglet right behind the exhaust, both aimed at shaving drag and giving the car a cleaner flow on the straights for this circuit. At the front, the lip has been reshaped to smooth the air coming into the car, helping the tyres get down‑force earlier in the corners. Together, these tweaks should boost top‑speed on the long runs while keeping the car stable through the twisty sections of this weekend’s track.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull’s mechanics have tweaked the rear‑wheel bodywork to improve its durability, and they’ve reshaped the little “floor bib” that sits where the floor meets the chassis. Both changes are aimed at preventing cracks or failures that could cost the team a pit stop or a retirement, giving the cars a more reliable platform for qualifying and the race. In short, the tweaks should keep the RB cars on track longer and let the drivers focus on speed rather than worrying about break‑downs.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has reshaped the fairing on the rear‑top wishbone, essentially fine‑tuning the rear suspension’s load handling. The tweak gives the car a more stable rear end, helping the tires stay in their sweet spot longer and improving cornering confidence. In short, you should see better grip out of the bends and a more consistent feel over the weekend’s races.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has added a new piece to the forward part of the floor board, essentially giving the car a little extra “bite” on the front edge. This tweak should boost front‑end grip and stability, helping the drivers get the car into the corner quicker and stay on the racing line. In short, it’s a small change that could translate into more consistent lap times and a better fight for points this weekend.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac has given the rear wing a new little winglet at the back edge and added a small fin inside the diffuser’s sidewall. Both tweaks generate extra push on the rear of the car, keeping the chassis planted and the tires more evenly loaded through fast corners. The result should be steadier handling and a better lap time right out of the box for this weekend’s race.
